desk.headline: Q3 revenue down 9% to RMB21.0bn but ahead of estimates (reported 16 Nov); adjusted profit doubles, beat; no guidance
results: The 16 November filing is a set of Hong Kong buyback returns, not results; KE reported Q3 results the same day.
Revenue fell 9% to RMB21.0bn as rental income shrank 25% (more homes now booked on a net basis) and renovation fell 23%; existing-home and new-home revenue each grew 2–3%.
Profit jumped: gross margin rose to 27.7% from 21.4%, and adjusted net income doubled to RMB2.61bn, or RMB2.35 per ADS against an estimate of about RMB1.71.
Every main business improved its contribution margin; rental rose to 16.6% from 8.7% and renovation to 40.2% from 32.0%.
KE bought back about $162m of stock in Q3 and kept buying in November (about $1.5–2.5m a day on the NYSE); cash and short-term investments were RMB64.0bn.

guidance.summary: KE gives no financial guidance; management only described the housing market and a step-by-step approach to new spending.

points: Management sees existing-home markets steadying, especially in big cities; tier-1 home prices rose 4.1% so far this year.
October deals in 50 tracked cities rose about 31% after a September mortgage subsidy, though the effect is still being judged.
New-home sales remain weak (down 13.7% in nine months) and reforms to off-plan sales may slow that market further.
Rental accounting changes cut reported revenue but lift profit; managed rental units grew 25% to about 830,000.
Digital tools are used to find buyers, flag rental renewals and train agents; new spending will be phased in and tested.

watch: Whether the September mortgage subsidy keeps lifting existing-home deals into Q4.
New-home sales and the impact of off-plan sales reform on KE's new-home commissions.
Whether rental and renovation revenue stop shrinking now that margins have improved.
